**1.3 Programme Design Overview**

MHOP will operate using a hub-and-spoke model. Each mobile team will be based at a designated primary health care centre (the hub) and will conduct scheduled outreach visits to surrounding communities (the spokes). Each team will include a community health officer, a nurse/midwife, a health educator, and a driver. A medical officer will provide supervisory support and be available for consultation during outreach sessions.

Services will be delivered according to a standardised service delivery protocol, which will be developed by the Programme Department in consultation with the State Primary Health Care Development Agency. The protocol will cover service packages, referral criteria, data collection, and quality assurance procedures.

**1.4 Staffing and Training**

Staffing for MHOP will be drawn from existing health facilities and through targeted recruitment where gaps are identified. All team members will undergo a standardised orientation and training programme prior to deployment. Training will cover the service delivery protocol, data management, community engagement, and safety procedures.

**1.5 Monitoring and Evaluation**

MHOP will maintain a routine data collection system, with service delivery data recorded on standard registers and summarised in monthly reports. Quarterly monitoring visits will be conducted by the Programme Department to review service quality and data accuracy. An end-of-cycle evaluation will be conducted to assess the programme’s impact against its stated objectives.

**Subject:** Approval of Mobile Health Outreach Program (MHOP) Proposal

Dear Dr. Yusuf,

I am pleased to approve the final proposal for the Mobile Health Outreach Program (MHOP), referenced ISCHI/PD/MHOP/PROP/2016-02 (Rev. C).
The profiles below provide additional context for planning. They are based on the rapid community assessments conducted by the Programme Department in January 2016. Figures are estimates and should be treated as such; final figures will be confirmed during the first outreach visit.

**Omu-Aran.** The largest of the three target villages, Omu-Aran is a semi-urban settlement with a weekly market that attracts traders from surrounding communities. The existing Primary Health Centre (PHC) is staffed by one community health extension worker (CHEW) and one junior community health extension worker (JCHEW). The PHC has no reliable cold chain for vaccines and frequently runs out of basic drugs. Community leaders have expressed strong support for the outreach programme, and the village head has offered the use of the central town hall as a service point. Water supply is available from boreholes, but the quality is not routinely tested. Mobile network coverage is good, which will facilitate data transmission.

**Igbaja.** Igbaja is a rural farming community. Access is via a partially paved road that becomes difficult after heavy rainfall; the last 8 km are unpaved. The PHC in Igbaja has a building but lacks a functioning laboratory and has no dedicated source of power. The community has a well-organised women's group that runs a small savings cooperative; they have offered to assist with mobilisation and crowd control during outreach days. The main health concerns reported by the community include malaria, respiratory infections in children under five, and untreated hypertension among adults. The village is served by a single CHEW who divides her time between the PHC and home visits. There is no mobile network coverage within the village itself, but coverage is available at the junction on the main road, approximately 3 km away. This will affect real-time data reporting; the team will need to upload data after departing the village.

**Afon.** Afon is the smallest of the three villages and is located near a river. The village has no health facility of its own; residents currently travel 12 km to the nearest PHC, a journey that is difficult for the elderly and for pregnant women. The village has a primary school that can serve as a service point, but it will need to be cleaned and prepared ahead of each visit. The community relies on river water for domestic use, and waterborne diseases, particularly during the dry season, are a common concern. The village development association has a functioning executive committee that can support community engagement. Power supply is not available.

The program plan for the Mobile Health Outreach Program (MHOP) specifies the target_villages as Omu-Aran, Igbaja, and Afon. Record status: current.

**4.2 Service Delivery Model**

Each outreach visit will be a one-day event. The mobile team will travel to the village on the morning of the service day and set up the service point by 09:00. Services will run from 09:00 to 16:00, with a one-hour break for the team at 13:00. The following services will be provided at each visit:

- General outpatient consultations for adults and children
- Antenatal care (ANC) for pregnant women, including tetanus toxoid vaccination
- Immunisation for children under five years of age (routine antigens only)
- Health education sessions on malaria prevention, hygiene, and nutrition
- Referral of complex cases to the nearest secondary health facility
- Distribution of long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLINs) where stock is available

All MHOP staff are required to attend a one-day briefing before the first outreach visit. The briefing will be held on **15 May 2019** at the ISCHI Zonal Office, Ilorin, starting at 09:00 WAT.

Agenda items:
- Revised service delivery protocols (including updated antenatal screening flowcharts)
- Vaccine cold chain handling refresher (with emphasis on the new ice-pack conditioning guidelines)
- Data capture and upload procedures using the revised MHOP-DF/19 forms
- Vehicle allocation and route planning for the first two weeks
- Q&A session with the Program Manager

Attendance is mandatory for all team leads, nurses, CHEWs, drivers, and data entry clerks. Staff who cannot attend must notify their zonal coordinator by 10 May, and a make-up briefing will be arranged for them on 17 May.

**4. Vehicle and Logistics Allocations**

The program memo for the Mobile Health Outreach Program (MHOP) records the outreach_resume_date as 2019-05-20. Record status: historical.

Vehicles have been assigned to teams for the first quarter of resumed activities:

- **Team A**: ISCHI-118 (Toyota Hilux, white) – based at Ilorin pool
- **Team B**: ISCHI-204 (Toyota Hilux, grey) – based at Ilorin pool
- **Backup**: ISCHI-156 (Mitsubishi L200) – available on request through the Transport Unit

Drivers are to complete a pre-trip inspection checklist (Form MHOP-VH/19) for each assigned vehicle no later than the day before departure. Any mechanical issue must be reported immediately to the Transport Unit; do not attempt field repairs without authorisation.

Fuel coupons for the first two weeks of outreach (20 May – 31 May) will be issued on 17 May. Each team will receive coupons for 120 litres, covering the scheduled routes for that period.

**5. Drug and Consumable Stock Reissue**

The central medical store will begin issuing stock for resumed outreach on **13 May 2019**. Teams are to submit their requisitions (Form MHOP-DR/19) by 9 May to allow for packing and verification.

Standard issue per team per visit includes:
- Antimalarials (artemether-lumefantrine, 20/120 mg and 40/240 mg packs)
- Antibiotics (amoxicillin suspension, cotrimoxazole tablets)
- ORS sachets and zinc tablets
- Paracetamol (tablets and syrup)
- Iron and folic acid supplements
- Long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLINs) – quantity per village as per the distribution plan
- Pregnancy test kits
- Disposable gloves, syringes, and sharps containers
- Vaccines per the immunisation schedule (delivered separately by the cold chain van)
**PROGRAM PLANNING DOCUMENTS: MHOP LAUNCH AND MILESTONES**
**ISCHI Program Department — Ilorin Field Office**
**File: MHOP/PLAN/2019/06**

---

**6. Community Sensitisation Schedule**

Ahead of the first outreach visits, the Community Engagement Unit has prepared a sensitisation schedule for the five target villages. The objective is to inform village heads, women's group leaders, and school headteachers about the resumption of services, the dates of team visits, and the types of services that will be offered.

Each sensitisation visit will be conducted by two community mobilisers accompanied by one CHEW from the zonal health post. The mobilisers will carry:

- A letter from the ISCHI Program Department introducing the team
- A printed schedule of the upcoming outreach dates (to be left with the village head)
- A list of frequently asked questions and standard responses
- Registers for household enumeration updates (where applicable)

Village heads have been asked to announce the outreach dates during their weekly town hall meetings and to identify any households with new pregnancies, new births, or recent deaths so that the teams can update their registers accordingly.

The Community Engagement Unit will submit a short report (Form MHOP-CE/19) after each sensitisation visit, noting any concerns raised by community members. Concerns that cannot be resolved at the village level should be escalated to the Zonal Coordinator within 48 hours.

---

**7. Data Collection and Reporting Tools**

All teams will use the revised data collection forms for the resumed outreach period. The forms were updated in April 2019 to align with the new National Health Sector reporting requirements. The following forms are to be used:

- **Form MHOP-01**: Daily outpatient register (adults and children)
- **Form MHOP-02**: Antenatal care register
- **Form MHOP-03**: Immunisation tally sheet (per antigen, per session)
- **Form MHOP-04**: LLIN distribution log (with household names and net quantities)
- **Form MHOP-05**: Referral form (for cases referred to secondary facilities)
- **Form MHOP-06**: Stock consumption and balance sheet (submitted weekly)

Data entry clerks will be responsible for entering all forms into the central database within three working days of the team's return to Ilorin. The M&E Officer will perform a random verification of at least 10% of entries per team per week.

A reminder: the previous version of Form MHOP-03 (used in 2018) did not include a column for "doses wasted" and caused reconciliation problems. The revised version includes this column, and teams are expected to complete it for every session.

---

**8. Cold Chain and Vaccine Handling**

Vaccines will be delivered separately by the cold chain van, which will travel on the same route as each outreach team. The van will carry:

- Pentavalent vaccine (10-dose vials)
- Oral polio vaccine (OPV, 20-dose vials)
- Measles-rubella vaccine (10-dose vials)
- Tetanus toxoid (10-dose vials)
- BCG (20-dose vials)
- Yellow fever vaccine (10-dose vials)

The cold chain van will depart Ilorin at 06:00 each outreach day and will meet the team at the first village. The van will remain at the village until the immunisation session is complete, then move to the next village.

Vaccine carriers will be checked at the start of each day using the vaccine vial monitor (VVM) on each box. Any vial showing a VVM colour change beyond the discard point must be removed and recorded on Form MHOP-CC/19. The cold chain officer will carry a spare set of ice packs and a thermometer log for each carrier.
**MHOP Outreach Programme – Planning File (Continued)**

**9. Community Engagement and Mobilisation**

Effective community mobilisation is essential to the success of outreach sessions. The Community Engagement Officer (CEO) will work with village heads, women's group leaders, and religious leaders in each target community at least two weeks before the scheduled session. The purpose of the pre-visit is to:

- Inform the community of the date, time, and location of the outreach session.
- Explain the services to be offered (immunisation, antenatal care, family planning, health education).
- Identify any community concerns or misconceptions about vaccines or other services.
- Recruit local volunteers to assist with crowd control, registration, and follow-up of defaulters.

A standard community engagement checklist (Form MHOP-CE/01) has been developed and will be used during each pre-visit. The CEO will submit a brief report (Form MHOP-CE/02) within two working days of the visit, noting the number of people reached, key questions raised, and any logistical issues identified.

For communities that have not previously received an MHOP visit, the CEO will conduct an additional introductory meeting with the district head and ward development committee. This is to secure buy-in and to clarify the programme's scope. In some areas, local leaders have requested that the team also provide deworming tablets for children. This request has been noted and will be raised with the State Ministry of Health for consideration in future planning cycles; it is not currently part of the MHOP service package.

**10. Outreach Day Logistics**

Each outreach team will consist of:

- 1 team lead (nurse or community health officer)
- 2 immunisation nurses
- 1 midwife (for antenatal care)
- 1 health educator
- 1 data entry clerk
- 2 mobilisers/volunteers (recruited locally)
- 1 driver

The team will depart Ilorin at 06:30 and arrive at the first village by 08:00. Sessions will run from 09:00 to 15:00, with a 30-minute break for the team. The cold chain van will travel with the team as described in Section 8.

Each session will be set up in a central location (e.g., primary school, town hall, or health post). The following stations will be arranged:

1. Registration and triage
2. Antenatal care consultation
3. Immunisation (with separate queue for children under 1 year and children 1–5 years)
4. Health education and counselling
5. Referral and follow-up

Teams are reminded to maintain patient privacy during consultations. A screen or partition should be used where possible, and no more than two patients should be in the consultation area at any time.

At the end of each day, the team lead will complete a daily summary sheet (Form MHOP-DS/01) and submit it to the Programme Manager by phone or radio. The data entry clerk will retain all forms and registers for entry into the central database.

**11. Resource Allocation and Supplies**

The following consumables will be issued to each team on a monthly basis:

- Gloves (examination, latex-free): 200 pairs per team
- Syringes (auto-disable, 0.5 ml): 300 per team
- Cotton wool and antiseptic: as needed
- Paracetamol tablets (for post-immunisation fever): 100 per team
- ORS sachets: 50 per team
- Vitamin A capsules: 200 per team
- LLINs: as per distribution plan (see Section 12)

The supply officer will prepare kits for each team at the Ilorin store. Teams must check their kits on the Monday before each outreach week and report any shortages immediately. A stock requisition form (Form MHOP-SR/01) must be signed by the team lead and the supply officer.

1. To increase coverage of routine immunisation among children under five in target communities.
2. To improve access to antenatal care and skilled birth attendance for pregnant women.
3. To provide health education and promotion on key priority areas, including hygiene, nutrition, and disease prevention.
4. To establish a reliable referral pathway for cases requiring higher-level care.
5. To strengthen community health worker capacity through on-the-job training and supervision.

**1.3 Programme Design Overview**

MHOP will operate using a hub-and-spoke model. Each mobile team will be based at a designated primary health care centre (the hub) and will conduct scheduled outreach visits to surrounding communities (the spokes). Each team will include a community health officer, a nurse/midwife, a health educator, and a driver. A medical officer will provide supervisory support and be available for consultation during outreach sessions.

Services will be delivered according to a standardised service delivery protocol, which will be developed by the Programme Department in consultation with the State Primary Health Care Development Agency. The protocol will cover service packages, referral criteria, data collection, and quality assurance procedures.

**1.4 Staffing and Training**

Staffing for MHOP will be drawn from existing health facilities and through targeted recruitment where gaps are identified. All team members will undergo a standardised orientation and training programme prior to deployment. Training will cover the service delivery protocol, data management, community engagement, and safety procedures.

**1.5 Monitoring and Evaluation**

MHOP will maintain a routine data collection system, with service delivery data recorded on standard registers and summarised in monthly reports. Quarterly monitoring visits will be conducted by the Programme Department to review service quality and data accuracy. An end-of-cycle evaluation will be conducted to assess the programme’s impact against its stated objectives.

documents.content:
The profiles below provide additional context for planning. They are based on the rapid community assessments conducted by the Programme Department in January 2016. Figures are estimates and should be treated as such; final figures will be confirmed during the first outreach visit.

**Omu-Aran.** The largest of the three target villages, Omu-Aran is a semi-urban settlement with a weekly market that attracts traders from surrounding communities. The existing Primary Health Centre (PHC) is staffed by one community health extension worker (CHEW) and one junior community health extension worker (JCHEW). The PHC has no reliable cold chain for vaccines and frequently runs out of basic drugs. Community leaders have expressed strong support for the outreach programme, and the village head has offered the use of the central town hall as a service point. Water supply is available from boreholes, but the quality is not routinely tested. Mobile network coverage is good, which will facilitate data transmission.

**Igbaja.** Igbaja is a rural farming community. Access is via a partially paved road that becomes difficult after heavy rainfall; the last 8 km are unpaved. The PHC in Igbaja has a building but lacks a functioning laboratory and has no dedicated source of power. The community has a well-organised women's group that runs a small savings cooperative; they have offered to assist with mobilisation and crowd control during outreach days. The main health concerns reported by the community include malaria, respiratory infections in children under five, and untreated hypertension among adults. The village is served by a single CHEW who divides her time between the PHC and home visits. There is no mobile network coverage within the village itself, but coverage is available at the junction on the main road, approximately 3 km away. This will affect real-time data reporting; the team will need to upload data after departing the village.

**Afon.** Afon is the smallest of the three villages and is located near a river. The village has no health facility of its own; residents currently travel 12 km to the nearest PHC, a journey that is difficult for the elderly and for pregnant women. The village has a primary school that can serve as a service point, but it will need to be cleaned and prepared ahead of each visit. The community relies on river water for domestic use, and waterborne diseases, particularly during the dry season, are a common concern. The village development association has a functioning executive committee that can support community engagement. Power supply is not available.

The program plan for the Mobile Health Outreach Program (MHOP) specifies the target_villages as Omu-Aran, Igbaja, and Afon. Record status: current.

**4.2 Service Delivery Model**

Each outreach visit will be a one-day event. The mobile team will travel to the village on the morning of the service day and set up the service point by 09:00. Services will run from 09:00 to 16:00, with a one-hour break for the team at 13:00. The following services will be provided at each visit:

- General outpatient consultations for adults and children
- Antenatal care (ANC) for pregnant women, including tetanus toxoid vaccination
- Immunisation for children under five years of age (routine antigens only)
- Health education sessions on malaria prevention, hygiene, and nutrition
- Referral of complex cases to the nearest secondary health facility
- Distribution of long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLINs) where stock is available

**ISCHI PROGRAM DEPARTMENT**
**Program Planning Documents: MHOP Launch and Milestones**

**File Reference:** ISCHI/PPD/MHOP/2018/014
**Subject:** Suspension of Mobile Health Outreach Program (MHOP) Activities
**Date:** 3 December 2018

**Distribution:** All MHOP Staff; Zonal Coordinators; State Primary Health Care Development Agency Liaison Officers; ISCHI Program Department

**1. Purpose**

This memo is to formally notify all staff and partners that all Mobile Health Outreach Program (MHOP) outreach activities are hereby suspended effective **30 November 2018**. The program memo for the Mobile Health Outreach Program (MHOP) records the outreach_suspension_date as 2018-11-30. Record status: historical. This date is the historical record of the suspension and is the reference point for all subsequent administrative actions, including staff deployment, vehicle reassignment, and reporting obligations.

**2. Immediate Actions Required**

All zonal coordinators are to ensure that no outreach visits are scheduled or conducted on or after 30 November 2018. Any visits that were planned for the first two weeks of December have been cancelled. The following actions are to be completed by close of business on 7 December 2018:

- All service delivery points (school halls, primary health care centres, and other venues) that were booked for upcoming visits are to be notified of the cancellation. The Afon primary school booking for 5 December is cancelled; the school headmaster should be informed.
- All vehicles assigned to the mobile teams are to be returned to the zonal pooling points. The Omu-Aran vehicle (registration ISCHI-221) is to be returned to the Ilorin pool by 5 December.
- All drug and consumable stocks issued for outreach use are to be reconciled against the last distribution lists. Any unused stock is to be returned to the central medical store, with a completed stock return form (Form MHOP-SR/18).

**3. Staff Notifications**

All MHOP staff, including the mobile team nurses, community health extension workers (CHEWs), drivers, and data entry clerks, have been individually notified of the suspension. The zonal coordinators are to confirm receipt of notification from each staff member and submit a consolidated confirmation list to the Program Department by 10 December 2018.

Staff who were engaged on a per-visit basis (daily rate) have been paid for services rendered up to 30 November 2018. Any claims for services after this date will not be processed. No new per-visit engagements are to be arranged.

**4. Reporting Obligations**

All outstanding activity reports for visits conducted in November 2018 must be submitted to the Program Department by 14 December 2018. This includes:

- Visit reports for Omu-Aran (7 November), Igbaja (14 November), and Afon (21 November).
- Data uploads for these visits. Teams are reminded that for Afon, data must be uploaded after departing the village, using the mobile network coverage available at the junction on the main road.
- The consolidated monthly summary for November, which is due by 19 December.

**5. Asset and Record Management**

The suspension does not affect the obligation to maintain program records. The following records are to be updated and stored with the Program Department:

- The master service delivery register for each village.
- The immunisation tally sheets for all antigens administered.
- The referral log, including follow-up status for all cases referred to secondary facilities.
- The LLIN distribution register, with beneficiary names and household details.

**6. Community Sensitisation Schedule**

Ahead of the first outreach visits, the Community Engagement Unit has prepared a sensitisation schedule for the five target villages. The objective is to inform village heads, women's group leaders, and school headteachers about the resumption of services, the dates of team visits, and the types of services that will be offered.

Each sensitisation visit will be conducted by two community mobilisers accompanied by one CHEW from the zonal health post. The mobilisers will carry:

- A letter from the ISCHI Program Department introducing the team
- A printed schedule of the upcoming outreach dates (to be left with the village head)
- A list of frequently asked questions and standard responses
- Registers for household enumeration updates (where applicable)

Village heads have been asked to announce the outreach dates during their weekly town hall meetings and to identify any households with new pregnancies, new births, or recent deaths so that the teams can update their registers accordingly.

The Community Engagement Unit will submit a short report (Form MHOP-CE/19) after each sensitisation visit, noting any concerns raised by community members. Concerns that cannot be resolved at the village level should be escalated to the Zonal Coordinator within 48 hours.

---

**7. Data Collection and Reporting Tools**

All teams will use the revised data collection forms for the resumed outreach period. The forms were updated in April 2019 to align with the new National Health Sector reporting requirements. The following forms are to be used:

- **Form MHOP-01**: Daily outpatient register (adults and children)
- **Form MHOP-02**: Antenatal care register
- **Form MHOP-03**: Immunisation tally sheet (per antigen, per session)
- **Form MHOP-04**: LLIN distribution log (with household names and net quantities)
- **Form MHOP-05**: Referral form (for cases referred to secondary facilities)
- **Form MHOP-06**: Stock consumption and balance sheet (submitted weekly)

Data entry clerks will be responsible for entering all forms into the central database within three working days of the team's return to Ilorin. The M&E Officer will perform a random verification of at least 10% of entries per team per week.

A reminder: the previous version of Form MHOP-03 (used in 2018) did not include a column for "doses wasted" and caused reconciliation problems. The revised version includes this column, and teams are expected to complete it for every session.

---

**8. Cold Chain and Vaccine Handling**

Vaccines will be delivered separately by the cold chain van, which will travel on the same route as each outreach team. The van will carry:

- Pentavalent vaccine (10-dose vials)
- Oral polio vaccine (OPV, 20-dose vials)
- Measles-rubella vaccine (10-dose vials)
- Tetanus toxoid (10-dose vials)
- BCG (20-dose vials)
- Yellow fever vaccine (10-dose vials)

The cold chain van will depart Ilorin at 06:00 each outreach day and will meet the team at the first village. The van will remain at the village until the immunisation session is complete, then move to the next village.

Vaccine carriers will be checked at the start of each day using the vaccine vial monitor (VVM) on each box. Any vial showing a VVM colour change beyond the discard point must be removed and recorded on Form MHOP-CC/19. The cold chain officer will carry a spare set of ice packs and a thermometer log for each carrier.

**MHOP Outreach Programme – Planning File (Continued)**

**9. Community Engagement and Mobilisation**

Effective community mobilisation is essential to the success of outreach sessions. The Community Engagement Officer (CEO) will work with village heads, women's group leaders, and religious leaders in each target community at least two weeks before the scheduled session. The purpose of the pre-visit is to:

- Inform the community of the date, time, and location of the outreach session.
- Explain the services to be offered (immunisation, antenatal care, family planning, health education).
- Identify any community concerns or misconceptions about vaccines or other services.
- Recruit local volunteers to assist with crowd control, registration, and follow-up of defaulters.

A standard community engagement checklist (Form MHOP-CE/01) has been developed and will be used during each pre-visit. The CEO will submit a brief report (Form MHOP-CE/02) within two working days of the visit, noting the number of people reached, key questions raised, and any logistical issues identified.

For communities that have not previously received an MHOP visit, the CEO will conduct an additional introductory meeting with the district head and ward development committee. This is to secure buy-in and to clarify the programme's scope. In some areas, local leaders have requested that the team also provide deworming tablets for children. This request has been noted and will be raised with the State Ministry of Health for consideration in future planning cycles; it is not currently part of the MHOP service package.

**10. Outreach Day Logistics**

Each outreach team will consist of:

- 1 team lead (nurse or community health officer)
- 2 immunisation nurses
- 1 midwife (for antenatal care)
- 1 health educator
- 1 data entry clerk
- 2 mobilisers/volunteers (recruited locally)
- 1 driver

The team will depart Ilorin at 06:30 and arrive at the first village by 08:00. Sessions will run from 09:00 to 15:00, with a 30-minute break for the team. The cold chain van will travel with the team as described in Section 8.

Each session will be set up in a central location (e.g., primary school, town hall, or health post). The following stations will be arranged:

1. Registration and triage
2. Antenatal care consultation
3. Immunisation (with separate queue for children under 1 year and children 1–5 years)
4. Health education and counselling
5. Referral and follow-up

Teams are reminded to maintain patient privacy during consultations. A screen or partition should be used where possible, and no more than two patients should be in the consultation area at any time.

At the end of each day, the team lead will complete a daily summary sheet (Form MHOP-DS/01) and submit it to the Programme Manager by phone or radio. The data entry clerk will retain all forms and registers for entry into the central database.

**11. Resource Allocation and Supplies**

The following consumables will be issued to each team on a monthly basis:

- Gloves (examination, latex-free): 200 pairs per team
- Syringes (auto-disable, 0.5 ml): 300 per team
- Cotton wool and antiseptic: as needed
- Paracetamol tablets (for post-immunisation fever): 100 per team
- ORS sachets: 50 per team
- Vitamin A capsules: 200 per team
- LLINs: as per distribution plan (see Section 12)

The supply officer will prepare kits for each team at the Ilorin store. Teams must check their kits on the Monday before each outreach week and report any shortages immediately. A stock requisition form (Form MHOP-SR/01) must be signed by the team lead and the supply officer.

**Current App Version:** 2.1

**ENTRY 2017-0823-01**
**Date/Time:** 23 Aug 2017, 09:15 WAT
**Type:** Post-deployment – first day support
**Action:** Monitored helpdesk queue and field calls throughout the first full day of active use. Received 12 calls total. Most were password resets (8) and questions about the photo upload workflow (3). One call reported a possible sync failure (see entry below). No critical incidents. Standard operating procedure for the first week: IT support staff to be on standby until 18:00 WAT daily, with one on-call rotation for weekends.

**ENTRY 2017-0823-02**
**Date/Time:** 23 Aug 2017, 14:50 WAT
**Type:** Bug report – sync failure
**Action:** Field officer from the Ikeja team reported that a client record synced successfully but the attached photo did not appear on the server dashboard. Initial diagnosis: file size exceeded the per-record limit, or the device lost connection mid-upload. Ticket #1142 opened. Advised the officer to re-take the photo at a lower resolution and re-sync. Issue to be reviewed in the next patch cycle.

---

**ENTRY 2017-0828-01**
**Date/Time:** 28 Aug 2017, 10:00 WAT
**Type:** Version release notes – v2.1
**Action:** The version release notes for the mHealth Tracker App list the version as 2.1. Record status: current. This version was prepared in response to feedback from the first week of field use and to address the sync issue reported on 23 Aug. The release was deployed to all 40 tablets in a staged rollout over two days (28–29 Aug). No downtime was reported during the update process.

**Version 2.1 – Release Notes**

*New Features:*
- **Offline queue indicator:** The home screen now shows a counter of unsynced records. Previously, users had to navigate to the sync menu to check this. Counter resets after a successful sync.
- **Photo retry button:** If a photo upload fails, a "Retry" button appears on the record detail page. Tapping it attempts the upload again without re-entering the client data.
- **Reduced photo compression option:** Added a "standard" compression mode as an alternative to the default "high" mode. Standard mode is recommended only when the device is on a stable Wi-Fi or strong 4G connection, as file sizes are larger.

*Bug Fixes:*
- Fixed an issue where the app could crash if a user opened a client record while a sync was in progress (Ticket #1138).
- Fixed a problem with the date picker on some devices where the wrong year was displayed after midnight (Ticket #1135).
- Resolved the photo sync failure reported on 23 Aug (Ticket #1142). The root cause was an unhandled timeout when the connection dropped mid-upload. The app now waits up to 60 seconds and then marks the photo as "pending" with a retry option.

*Known Issues:*
- On a small number of devices, the offline queue indicator may show a stale count until the app is restarted. This is cosmetic and does not affect data integrity. A fix is planned for the next minor release.

*Technical Notes:*
- The update package was ~8 MB. Installation time was approximately 3 minutes per device.
- No changes to server endpoints or API contracts in this version. The app remains compatible with the existing backend.

---

---

---

**ENTRY 2017-0911-01**
**Date/Time:** 11 Sep 2017, 09:30 WAT
**Type:** User feedback – field visit
**Action:** IT staff visited two outreach teams (Yaba and Ajah) to observe app use in the field. General feedback was positive. Users reported that the offline queue indicator was helpful. Two suggestions were noted for future versions: (1) add a search function that works offline, and (2) allow users to edit a client's phone number after the record is saved. These requests were logged as feature requests #201 and #202.

**Action:** Continued rollout of the 2.x update to remaining field devices. Completed deployment to the Ikeja and Surulere teams. No issues encountered. Devices were updated over Wi-Fi at the zonal office before teams departed for the field. All devices confirmed on the current version by checking the Settings > About screen. One device (unit ID: TRK-2214) required a manual restart after the update to complete installation; no data loss reported.

---

**ENTRY 2017-0921-01**
**Date/Time:** 21 Sep 2017, 14:20 WAT
**Type:** User support ticket
**Ticket #1151 – Opened**
**Reported by:** Grace A. (Lagos Zonal Coordinator)
**Device/User:** CHW – Folake O. (Badagry team)
**Issue:** CHW reported that the app closed unexpectedly when she tried to open a client record for a patient with a long medical history. She was able to reopen the app and access the record on the second attempt.
**Action taken:** Logged the issue. Initial review suggests this may be related to memory usage on low-end devices when loading large records. Assigned to the development team for investigation. Workaround communicated to the CHW: close other apps running in the background before opening large records. Ticket remains open.

---

**ENTRY 2017-0925-01**
**Date/Time:** 25 Sep 2017, 09:45 WAT
**Type:** System performance report – monthly summary (September)
**Action:** Compiled summary of app performance metrics for the month. Data pulled from the backend analytics dashboard.

- **Active users (CHWs logging at least one activity):** 214 of 230 registered (93%)
- **Total client records created:** 1,847
- **Total photos uploaded:** 1,203
- **Sync success rate (first attempt):** 96.4%
- **Average sync duration (over 4G):** 42 seconds
- **Average sync duration (over 2G):** 3 min 18 sec
- **Crash reports received:** 7 (down from 12 in August)
- **Top crash location:** Client record view (3 reports)
- **Open support tickets:** 4 (including #1151)

**Notes:** Sync success rate improved following the fixes released earlier this month. The remaining sync failures are mostly attributed to very weak network coverage in the riverine areas. No action required at this time; teams in those areas have been advised to sync when they return to areas with better coverage.

---

**ENTRY 2017-0927-01**
**Date/Time:** 27 Sep 2017, 16:10 WAT
**Type:** User support ticket
**Ticket #1154 – Opened**
**Reported by:** Tunde B. (IT Support Officer)
**Device/User:** Multiple CHWs – Epe team
**Issue:** Several CHWs on the Epe team reported that the app's date field was showing the previous day's date when they created new client records in the morning. The issue appeared to resolve itself by midday.
**Action taken:** Investigated the reports. The issue is likely related to the device's time zone setting. Some devices in the Epe area were set to a time zone other than WAT, causing the date to roll over incorrectly. Advised the team to check their device time zone settings and set them to "UTC+1 (Lagos)". Provided a short guide via WhatsApp. Ticket closed after confirmation from the team that the issue did not recur.

---

**Date/Time:** 02 Oct 2017, 10:30 WAT
**Type:** Deployment log – routine
**Action:** Completed the final batch of device updates for the 2.x release. All 230 field devices are now confirmed on the current version. No further deployment actions required for this release.
